root_idea.summary: The root has two principal orientations: a vow or wager that binds or challenges a person, and a vocal sound such as wailing or coughing.
root_idea.development: The vow-and-risk branch extends to contest before a judge, strenuous persistence, determined travel, and the idiomatic fulfillment or completion of one's term. The separate sound branch yields loud weeping and the cough of camels.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested nominal lexical item and is displayed under the normalized citation form نَحْبٌ.

senses.definition: A binding vow or obligation, especially the vow fulfilled in قَضَى نَحْبَهُ.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is in the construction قَضَى نَحْبَهُ, literally understood as fulfilling or completing a binding vow.

senses.definition: Death or completion of one's life-term, as an idiomatic interpretation of قَضَى نَحْبَهُ.
senses.usage_conditions: In this Quranic construction, the expression may denote dying, being slain, ending one's days, or yielding one's soul; some lexical explanations phrase the completion as accomplishing one's want.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vow, make a vow, or bind oneself to an undertaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lay a bet or wager.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the verbal noun نَحْبٌ is also used in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise one's voice in weeping or wailing; to weep or wail intensely or with a prolonged voice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative vocal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cough.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested subject in this sense is a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel or journey at a quick or light pace, with exertion and perseverance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb describing strenuous, determined travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exert oneself energetically in work or to undertake and pursue a journey laboriously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; used for strenuous work and determined travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a journey, to harass or wear down a person by its length.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or figurative construction in which a long journey produces the hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To apply oneself to a matter and persist in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported with عَلَى أَمْرٍ and فِي أَمْرٍ constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lay a wager with another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To refer a dispute to a judge or umpire, or to contend with another for honor or superiority before one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III; the judicial or adjudicative setting is part of the reported construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To agree together on a time, especially a time for fighting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI; the appointed time may also be for another purpose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sigh vehemently, or to weep and sigh vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great bet or wager.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use, distinct from the binding-vow sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proof, demonstration, or piece of evidence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A necessity, want, needful thing, or object of need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The soul or self.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal synonymic use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mind, purpose, aspiration, desire, or ambition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use for a person's purpose or motivating aspiration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A laborious journey or a quick, energetic pace of travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in journey and pace expressions; the same epithet may be applied to a person who travels in this manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Length or an extended span of time; a long day, period, or fixed term.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use for temporal extent or duration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sleep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal synonymic use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fatness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehemence, violence, distress, difficulty, or adversity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use, reported as equivalent to شِدَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A game of hazard or gambling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal use, equivalent to قِمَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A doubtful lexical report; it is noted as possibly being an error for نَجْبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lot used for drawing lots, or sortilege itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Feminine noun; the sense is associated with deciding or adjudicating a matter by lot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cough that affects camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Animal-specific noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female wailer; a woman who weeps or wails.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Feminine noun, with the plural نَوَاحِبُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who proceeds in a direct, determined course, as though bound by a vow; by extension, a journey characterized by such determined or laborious travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active-participial use in the expression سَارَ سَيْرًا مُنَحِّبًا.

cautions: The sole Quranic occurrence is the idiom قَضَى نَحْبَهُ; its lexical interpretation ranges from fulfilling a vow to dying or completing one's life-term, so translations may differ.
The reported sense نَحْبٌ 'a great camel' is explicitly treated as possibly an error for نَجْبٌ.
